extracted.intended_audience: GCC government policymakers, national IP offices, legislators, and stakeholders involved in IP law and economic diversification
extracted.subtask_description: Recommendations and standards for modernizing GCC intellectual property laws and institutions (patents, trademarks, industrial designs, geographical indications, plant varieties) based on EU best practice and WIPO instruments. Aimed at guiding accession to treaties, administrative reforms, and innovation policy alignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Madrid Agreement (repression of false or deceptive indications of source)
rubrics_metrics.description: All goods bearing a false or deceptive indication of source must be seized on importation, or such importation must be prohibited, or other actions and sanctions applied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Agreement provides remedies such as seizure and prohibition of importation and prohibits use of publicity capable of deceiving the public as to source. In the absence of effective national GI protection, GCC Member States are recommended to join the Madrid Agreement to serve as an enforcement tool for GIs entering the GCC market including European GIs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Madrid Protocol (international registration of marks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Permits international registration on the basis of a national application (instead of national registration) and alleviates consequences of the 'central attack system' by preserving national trademarks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended that Saudi Arabia, Qatar, UAE and Kuwait ratify the Protocol to modernize and make trademark protection more efficient, reducing cost and time for applicants and allowing protection in up to 107 countries via a single international registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt Singapore Treaty provisions for trademark procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Create an effective international framework harmonizing administrative trademark registration procedures; recognizes non-traditional marks; requires multiclass applications and use of the International Nice Classification; prohibits requiring authentication/certification/attestation of any signature on paper communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adherence will modernize systems, resolve procedural difficulties (e.g., elimination of single-class-per-application and removal of legalization requirements), and harmonize procedures with other signatory countries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with Washington Treaty provisions for layout-designs (via TRIPS Article 35)
rubrics_metrics.description: Protection of layout-designs of integrated circuits: Article 35 of TRIPS requires Members to comply with certain provisions of the Treaty on Intellectual Property in Respect of Integrated Circuits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the Washington Treaty is not in force, its main provisions are incorporated by reference into TRIPS and thus mandatory for GCC countries to comply with regarding layout-design protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership of PCT and use of international patent cooperation tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Participation in the Patent Cooperation Treaty (PCT) to facilitate international patent filings and cooperation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All GCC countries are PCT members; using the PCT system supports international patent protection strategies and harmonized procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accession to the Budapest Treaty (deposit of microorganisms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognition of the deposit of microorganisms for the purposes of patent procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Four GCC countries (Bahrain, Saudi Arabia, Oman and Qatar) are members; accession facilitates patent prosecution in biotech fields where deposits are required for sufficiency/enablement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accession to the Hague Agreement for international industrial design registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Obtain protection in designated Contracting States by filing a single international application in one language, paying one set of fees, in one currency, filed with one office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adherence will improve the IP framework, encourage creativity (e.g., fashion), and attract foreign investors and creators; Oman has joined, others are encouraged to follow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of geographical indications and appellations of origin (Lisbon Agreement / Geneva Act)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt systems for protection and international registration of appellations of origin and GIs, and consider accession to the Geneva Act of the Lisbon Agreement once adequate GI protection systems exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: None of the GCC countries had joined the Lisbon Agreement; accession (Oman has issued a decree for accession to the Geneva Act) would strengthen GI protection and international recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt international classification agreements (Nice, Locarno, Strasbourg, Vienna)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the international classification systems for goods, services, industrial designs, patents and figurative elements of marks to harmonize filings and registrations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although many GCC offices adopt these classifications de facto, formal accession (some recent Saudi and Bahrain accessions noted) will standardize practice, enable multiclass filings, and reduce procedural friction for national and foreign applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure TRIPS compliance and respect non-discrimination obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: As WTO members, GCC states must protect IP rights at least at the level provided by TRIPS and honor national treatment and most‑favoured‑nation principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Laws should be updated to meet TRIPS minimum standards; membership binds countries to the TRIPS objectives and obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine plant variety protection regime consistent with TRIPS Article 27.3(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Countries are free to protect plant varieties by patents, an effective sui generis system, or any combination thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decision should balance community interests, farmers’ rights, and biodiversity; Saudi Arabia chose patents for plant varieties, while Kuwait and Qatar exclude plant varieties from patentability and are potential UPOV candidates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider accession to UPOV when excluding plant varieties from patentability
rubrics_metrics.description: Join the International Union for the Protection of New Varieties of Plants (UPOV) when the national regime favors sui generis protection for plant varieties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oman and Bahrain are UPOV members; accession is appropriate if the national legal framework excludes plant varieties from patentability and seeks standardized breeders’ rights protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Join and implement CBD and Nagoya Protocol obligations where applicable
rubrics_metrics.description: Membership and compliance with the Convention on Biological Diversity and the Nagoya Protocol on Access and Benefit Sharing affect access to genetic resources and related IP considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most GCC states are members (Bahrain excepted for Nagoya); these instruments interact with patenting of biological inventions and require ABS-compliant practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invest in human capital to make IP protection effective
rubrics_metrics.description: High levels of human capital are necessary for IP to foster innovation rather than imitation; education, skills, and research capacity underpin a knowledge-based economy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt strategies such as early childhood development, better education and training, lifelong learning, female labor force participation, and multisectoral investments as recommended by the World Bank to complement IP reforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strengthen administrative infrastructure and capacity building in IP offices
rubrics_metrics.description: Legislative changes must be accompanied by administrative reforms and capacity building of human resources to implement commitments effectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Without modern infrastructure and trained personnel, importing high‑standard laws (e.g., FTA-driven changes) will not yield effective protection; focus on institutional reforms and training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish and support technology transfer offices, national research councils, and R&D funding mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Create institutions (TTOs, research councils, science parks, national research funds) and programs to promote technology transfer, commercialization, and R&D.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include Qatar Science & Technology Park, Research Councils in Oman, TTOs in universities, NSTIP in Saudi Arabia, and Khalifa University’s tech transfer strategy; these institutions are essential for turning IP into economic value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt the Innovation Principle and innovation-friendly regulatory policy
rubrics_metrics.description: When regulations are under consideration, assess and address their impact on innovation to create the best possible conditions for innovation to flourish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GCC countries should design legislation that supports innovation (e.g., UAE’s RegLab) and promote dialogue between industry, policymakers and stakeholders to ensure regulations are innovation-friendly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use EU models such as Horizon 2020 lessons and EC Regulation on Transfer of Technology
rubrics_metrics.description: Learn from EU programmes (Horizon 2020) and the EC Transfer of Technology Regulation (TTBER and Guidelines) concerning competition assessment of technology transfer agreements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Horizon 2020 illustrates coupling research and innovation, creating networks and infrastructure; EC TTBER offers a model for assessing licensing and technology transfer arrangements in competition law that GCC countries may adapt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance IP incentives with public interest and TRIPS flexibilities (public health, access to knowledge)
rubrics_metrics.description: IP policy should incentivize innovation while respecting social welfare, public health needs and access to knowledge, preserving applicable TRIPS flexibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementation of ambitious national visions should not preclude use of TRIPS flexibilities for public health or access to information; policy must strike a balance between private incentives and public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eliminate burdensome procedural requirements (document legalization, single-class filings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Remove procedural obstacles such as legalization requirements for submitted documents and the restriction to a single class per trademark application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisions of the Singapore Treaty (e.g., prohibition on requiring authentication/certification of signatures and multiclass applications under Nice classification) should be adopted to reduce procedural difficulties for applicants.
